text: Beyond Visual Quality: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Cartoonization Quality Preservation and Recognition Robustness Under JPEG Compression

Image cartoonization changes the appearance of photographs, but visual appearance alone does not establish whether transformed images preserve information useful for machine recognition. This study evaluates OpenCV cartoonization, pretrained AnimeGANv2, and a Stable Diffusion image-to-image pipeline using a matched set of 3,925 Imagenette images across ten classes. Recognition is measured using two ResNet18 classifiers: a standard classifier and a JPEG-augmented classifier. Four image conditions—original, OpenCV, AnimeGANv2, and Stable Diffusion—are evaluated in an uncompressed setting and at JPEG quality settings 95, 75, 50, and 25. Outcomes include Top-1 accuracy, macro-F1, balanced accuracy, prediction consistency, paired statistical comparisons, and PSNR/SSIM for JPEG-related distortion. The results show differences in recognition performance across transformation conditions and classifier configurations. Visual distortion metrics are interpreted relative to the corresponding decoded image, not as direct measures of cartoonization fidelity to the original photograph. Conclusions are limited to the selected dataset, pipelines, and classifiers.
Keywords: image cartoonization; AnimeGANv2; Stable Diffusion; OpenCV; ResNet18; JPEG compression; image recognition; robustness; PSNR; SSIM

This study compares three cartoonization pipelines against original images and evaluates recognition under multiple JPEG quality settings. It also examines prediction consistency, class-level outcomes, image distortion metrics, and exploratory associations between image descriptors and classification correctness.
RQ2: How does JPEG quality relate to recognition performance and prediction changes?
RQ3: How do PSNR and SSIM vary across image conditions and JPEG quality settings?

The matched manifest contains 3,925 unique image records covering ten Imagenette classes. Each image is evaluated under four conditions: original, OpenCV cartoonization, AnimeGANv2, and Stable Diffusion. The tested compression settings are uncompressed, JPEG Q95, Q75, Q50, and Q25.

The evaluated methods are OpenCV-based cartoonization, pretrained AnimeGANv2, and Stable Diffusion 1.5 image-to-image transformation. The recorded Stable Diffusion configuration uses 512 × 512 processing, strength 0.45, guidance scale 7.5, 20 inference steps, an empty prompt, FP16, deterministic per-image seeds, and a disabled safety checker. Exact checkpoint revisions, source repositories, and licenses must be verified from the experiment records.

Two ResNet18 classifiers are evaluated: a standard classifier and a JPEG-augmented classifier. The recorded inference preprocessing uses Resize(256), CenterCrop(224), and ImageNet normalization. The final paper must additionally document the training split, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, augmentation implementation, checkpoint-selection rule, and software versions from the original experiment notebook.

Recognition metrics include Top-1 accuracy, macro-F1, balanced accuracy, and mean confidence. Prediction-flip summaries measure changes in predicted labels. PSNR and SSIM summarize JPEG distortion relative to the corresponding decoded image; they are not direct measures of perceptual quality or fidelity to the original photograph. Saved statistical outputs include paired bootstrap confidence intervals, paired McNemar tests with Holm correction, per-class metrics, and class-adjusted logistic associations for image descriptors. Descriptor associations are interpreted as associations, not causal effects.

Recognition outcomes should be interpreted as evidence about the evaluated pipelines under this particular experimental protocol, not as a universal ranking of cartoonization methods. Differences between the two classifiers may reflect different sensitivities to transformed image characteristics. The effects of JPEG compression should be assessed by comparing each quality setting with its corresponding uncompressed condition and consulting the paired statistical outputs.
PSNR and SSIM do not fully capture perceptual quality or semantic preservation.
Literature novelty, dataset licensing, model licenses, citations, and full implementation details require final verification.

This study provides a matched comparison of original and cartoonized images under multiple JPEG quality settings using standard and JPEG-augmented ResNet18 classifiers. It jointly examines downstream recognition, compression distortion, prediction consistency, class-level outcomes, and exploratory descriptor associations. Conclusions should remain limited to the tested dataset and implementations until further validation across datasets, architectures, and independent random seeds is conducted.
